title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with Python
text:
Comparing species
Next, I calculate the average body mass and flipper length for each penguin species. This allows us to compare the typical size of the three species.

species_summary = (
    penguins.groupby("species")
    .agg(
        average_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        average_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean")
    )
    .round(2)
)

The summary shows that the three species differ in both average body mass and average flipper length.

title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with Python
text:
Body mass and flipper length
Finally, I visualize the relationship between flipper length and body mass for each penguin species.

for species in penguins["species"].dropna().unique():
    subset = penguins[penguins["species"] == species]
    plt.scatter(
        subset["flipper_length_mm"],
        subset["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7
    )

plt.xlabel("Flipper Length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)")
plt.title("Penguin Body Mass vs. Flipper Length")
plt.legend(title="Species")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Body mass and flipper length of Palmer Penguins by species.





The plot shows a positive relationship between flipper length and body mass. Penguins with longer flippers generally have greater body mass. Gentoo penguins also tend to be larger than Adelie and Chinstrap penguins in these measurements.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
MDS Orientation


I’ve had a pretty good start at MDS. Orientation was pretty fun, it was nice to meet my classmates and play some games. There was a lot of information as well, some helpful, some more itimidating, but it was nice to get a better understading of the program. My favourite part was the scavenger goose chase activity, it was pretty fun and good to learn where my classes would be.
First week of class was pretty good as well. I was a bit unsure after the first day or two, because all of the github stuff is new to me and I was just confused on how it all worked. I also have a limited history of using terminal so this has been a bit of an adjustment. But now I’m already feeling much better about it. Most of the assignments last week went pretty well.
Now I’m just starting this week. I’m feeling better going into it, I just need to make sure I am prepared for quiz week next week by getting my work done early and leaving extra time to study, especially with class on friday this week.

title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with R
text:
Comparing species
Next, I calculate the average body mass and flipper length for each penguin species. This allows us to compare the typical size of the three species.

species_summary <- penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(
    average_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    average_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

The summary shows that the three species differ in both average body mass and average flipper length.

title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with R
text:
Body mass and flipper length
Finally, I visualize the relationship between flipper length and body mass for each penguin species.

ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(
    x = flipper_length_mm,
    y = body_mass_g,
    color = species
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    x = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    y = "Body Mass (g)",
    color = "Species",
    title = "Penguin Body Mass vs. Flipper Length"
  )
